intro: To follow a story, separate the background, the main events and what had happened before.
p.el cuaderno.consejo: It is masculine: «un cuaderno azul». Do not confuse it with «el cuadro», which is a painting.
p.el vecino.consejo: For a woman it is «la vecina». The «v» sounds like a «b».
p.el ascensor.consejo: In Latin America «el elevador» is also said. It is written with «sc», but sounds «s-th».
p.la mudanza.consejo: It comes from «mudarse». You say «hacer una mudanza».
p.la llave.consejo: The «ll» sounds like a «y»: «YA-be». It is feminine: «la llave».
p.mudarse.consejo: It takes «se»: «me mudo», «te mudas». The destination goes with «a»: «mudarse a Madrid».
p.reconocer.consejo: It only changes in «yo»: «reconozco». The other forms are regular.
p.aquel día.consejo: «Aquel» points to something distant in time. «Ese día» is closer.
p.al día siguiente.consejo: It is used when telling the past: «al día siguiente me levanté tarde».
p.desde entonces.consejo: It usually goes with the perfect when the fact reaches today: «desde entonces hemos hablado mucho».
p.mientras.consejo: It links two actions that happen at the same time: «mientras buscaba las llaves, encontró…».
p.hacía años.consejo: With «hacía» you count time from a moment in the past: «vivía allí desde hacía años».
b1.titulo: Track the time of each event
b1.texto:
A story has several time «lines»:

- The **imperfecto** sets the **background** or what repeats: **vivía** en el mismo edificio.
- The **indefinido** moves the **main events** forward: **encontró** un cuaderno.
- The **pluscuamperfecto** marks what had already happened **earlier**: alguien **había escrito** su nombre.
- The **perfecto** links an experience with the present: desde entonces **han hablado** muchas veces.

Also watch the time expressions: **hacía años**, **mientras**, **aquel día**, **al día siguiente**, **desde entonces**.
b2.f0.texto: How did you get to know your neighbour?
b2.f1.texto: I had been living in that building for years.
b2.f2.texto: And did you never greet him?
b2.f3.texto: I only said hello to him in the lift.
b2.f5.texto: One afternoon I found his blue notebook next to the door.
b2.f7.texto: He had lost it during the move.
b2.f8.texto: Since then you have talked many times.
b4.texto:
- **vivía**, **saludaba**, **olía**: imperfecto, for the background and habits.
- **encontró**, **llamó**, **reconoció**: indefinido, for the events that move the story along.
- **había escrito**, **había perdido**: pluscuamperfecto, for what happened before another past event.
- **han hablado**, **hemos hablado**: perfecto, for what reaches the present.

With **mientras**, the imperfecto usually marks the background action and the indefinido the one that interrupts: **Mientras buscaba** las llaves, **encontró** un cuaderno.
b4.e0.texto: Clara had been living in the same building for years.
b4.e1.texto: While she was looking for her keys, she found a blue notebook.
b4.e2.texto: Someone had written her name on the first page.
b5.f0.texto: For years, Clara greeted an almost unknown neighbour in the lift.
b5.f1.texto: The building always smelled of dust and onion soup.
b5.f2.texto: One afternoon, while she was looking for her keys, she found a blue notebook next to the lift.
b5.f3.texto: When she opened it, she saw that someone had written her name on the first page.
b5.f4.texto: Clara felt a small jolt in her chest and closed the notebook carefully.
b5.f5.texto: She knocked on the door of the neighbour, who had moved there only recently.
b5.f6.texto: The man recognised the notebook and smiled with relief.
b5.f7.texto: He had lost it during the move and no longer expected to see it again.
b5.f8.texto: The next day, he left a thank-you note under Clara's door.
b5.f9.texto: Since that day, the two neighbours have talked many times in the corridor.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it: the background action goes in the imperfect, «buscaba».
b6.o1.refuerzo: That happened after finding the notebook.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The move was the neighbour's, and before this moment.
b6.pregunta: What was Clara doing when she found the notebook?
b7.o0.refuerzo: The imperfect describes a background, not an earlier completed event.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the loss happened before the discovery, so it takes the pluperfect.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The future does not fit in a story about the past.
b7.pregunta: The neighbour lost the notebook earlier. Which form is missing?
b8.frase: Alguien había escrito su nombre en la página
b8.traduccion: Someone had written her name on the page
b9.o0.refuerzo: It is a single completed event, not a background.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is an earlier event, not the continuing background.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it: the imperfect describes a continuing situation.
b9.pregunta: Which form sets the background of the story?
b10.frase: Desde aquel día ellos ____ muchas veces.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the perfect links the past with the present.
b10.o1.refuerzo: The indefinido closes the action; here it continues until today.
b10.o2.refuerzo: The pluperfect looks at an earlier past, not at the present.
b10.pregunta: It is an experience that reaches today. Which form is missing?
b12.o0: Que vivía allí desde mucho antes.
b12.o0.refuerzo: That's it: «desde hacía años» counts time backwards.
b12.o1.refuerzo: On the contrary: he had been living there for a long time.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It does not talk about the future, but about a long past.
b12.pregunta: What does «vivía allí desde hacía años» show?
p.conociste.glosa: you met, you got to know (from «conocer»)
p.conociste.consejo: Indefinido of «conocer» with «tú». «Conocer a alguien» takes «a»: «conociste a tu vecino».
p.saludabas.consejo: Imperfect of «saludar» with «tú»: ending «-abas». It describes what you used to do.
p.cambió.consejo: Indefinido of «cambiar» with «él» or «ella»: the accent mark on the «ó». Present: «cambia».
p.cuaderno.consejo: It is masculine: «el cuaderno». The «cu» sounds «kw»: «kwa-DER-no».
p.habéis.consejo: Present of «haber» with «vosotros»: «habéis hablado». It is used mainly in Spain.
p.hablado.consejo: Participle of «hablar», regular: «habl-» + «-ado». The «h» is silent. It does not change.
p.buscaba.consejo: Imperfect of «buscar» with «yo», «él» or «ella»: ending «-aba». It is the background action.
p.encontró.consejo: Indefinido of «encontrar» with «él» or «ella»: the accent mark on the «ó». It is the main event.
p.saludaba.consejo: Imperfect of «saludar»: ending «-aba». It describes a habit in the past.
p.cebolla.consejo: It is feminine: «la cebolla». The «c» before «e» sounds «th» and the «ll» sounds «y».
p.abrirlo.consejo: It is «abrir» + «lo»: the pronoun joins the infinitive. «Al abrirlo» means when she opened it.
p.vio.consejo: Indefinido of «ver» with «él» or «ella». It has one syllable, so no accent mark. The «v» sounds like «b».
p.sintió.consejo: Indefinido of «sentir» with «él» or «ella»: the «e» becomes «i» and it has an accent mark on the «ó».
p.vuelco.consejo: It is masculine. «Dar un vuelco el corazón» means the heart skips a beat. It comes from «volcar».
p.cerró.consejo: Indefinido of «cerrar» with «él» or «ella»: regular, with an accent mark on the «ó». The «rr» is strong.
p.llamó.consejo: Indefinido of «llamar» with «él» or «ella»: the accent mark on the «ó». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.mudado.consejo: Participle of «mudarse», regular. «Se había mudado» means he had moved house.
p.hacía.consejo: In «hacía poco» it measures time back from a past moment: «hacía poco» means a short time before.
p.reconoció.consejo: Indefinido of «reconocer» with «él» or «ella»: the accent mark on the «ó». Present: «reconoce».
p.sonrió.consejo: Indefinido of «sonreír» with «él» or «ella»: the «i» of the ending is lost, and the accent mark falls on the «ó». The «rr» is strong.
p.dejó.consejo: Indefinido of «dejar» with «él» or «ella»: the accent mark on the «ó». Present: «deja». The «j» sounds like «h».
p.agradecimiento.consejo: It is masculine: «el agradecimiento». It comes from «agradecer». «Una nota de agradecimiento» is a thank-you note.
